key_insight: ~1 nm 2D sheets with ~1.8 eV gaps allow sub-10 nm tiers, 5-8x tighter than 3D NAND's ~45 nm. Workaround: 2D or oxide channels at 20-30 nm pitch, 100-200 tiers.
killer_doubt: 1000 wafer-scale 2D growths at 99.9% per-tier yield leave 37% good stacks; 6 nm steps need +/-3 nm contact landing; no gain-cell storage node fits 6 nm.
decisive_experiment: Grow a 10-tier MoS2/Al2O3 stack at <=450 C and 6-10 nm pitch on 200 mm; map per-tier continuity and mobility through staircase contacts; measure one vertical-gate cell per tier at 85 C.
prior_art: MIT (J. Kim group) low-temperature monolithic 3D TMD stacks, Nature 2024 (training knowledge); Macronix vertical-gate NAND geometry; Phase B N-28.

key_insight: Charge moves through a semiconductor channel, so endurance is unlimited; one sense amp per 128-bit string, no per-bit contact. Family member: one dossier with I-04670/I-01064.
killer_doubt: 128 tiers x 3 phases = 384 transfers: imec planar IGZO CTE >98% keeps 0.98^384 ~4e-4; need >=0.9997. Word-plane RC turns 60-130 ns into ~us.
decisive_experiment: University 16-32-tier vertical GAA CCD, IGZO versus poly-Si channel: CTE versus clock (1-100 MHz) at 25-85 C; kill if CTE <0.9995 at >=10 MHz.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024 planar; first vertical 3D CCD 2026, via search snippet, logged R16); 1970s Si CCD memories; Phase B N-08.

key_insight: Heavy-metal core gives circumferential spin-Hall polarisation (z x r = phi), collinear with ring bits: field-free SOT writes, unlimited endurance. Workaround read: radial TMR to the word plane.
killer_doubt: A 125x50x5 nm ring segment (3e-23 m3) needs Hk >=~160 Oe for 50 kT; axial read sees ~0.4 ohm GMR per bit on a ~1 kohm string: microvolt signals.
decisive_experiment: Plate or ALD CoFeB/Cu/CoFe shells in AAO pores around W cores (~$200k): measure circumferential switching current, Hk and thermal stability versus thickness, and axial versus radial MR per segment.
prior_art: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, 1960s); Parkin racetrack; cylindrical nanotube domain walls; Phase B N-82; sibling I-08865 dropped on its AMR read.

key_insight: Antifuse filaments have no read disturb or retention drift, so write-once decks suit weights read ~1e9 times a year; programming 280 Gb takes minutes.
killer_doubt: An 8-deck crosspoint at F=20 nm is ~5 Gb/mm2, ~4x below rewritable 200+-layer NAND (~20 Gb/mm2); models churn every 3-12 months; poly-diode decks exceed 400 C over logic.
decisive_experiment: Spreadsheet first (~$0): $/GB-year of 8-deck antifuse versus pSLC high-bandwidth flash under 6-12-month model churn; only if it wins, a BEOL oxide-diode antifuse test deck.
prior_art: Matrix/SanDisk 3D OTP (2001-05); Sandisk High Bandwidth Flash for weights (2025); Taalas hard-wired model chips; ROM-based compute-in-memory (training knowledge).

key_insight: Pre-latch gain is the right lever: ~100x charge gain would let a 0.1 fF (~600 e-) cell drive a few-fF local line.
killer_doubt: Si junctions avalanche at >=~6-10 V with ~10-20 mV/K Vbr drift, so gain spreads exponentially; 0.1 fF held 64 ms needs <=0.16 fA, ~80x below the 13 fA tail.
decisive_experiment: Superseded by SPICE against N-04 charge-transfer sensing. If pursued: 65 nm MPW of vertical junctions at 30-100 nm pitch, measuring gain spread, dark counts and afterpulsing at 25-85 C.
prior_art: SPAD and quanta image sensors; Z-RAM impact ionisation; EMCCD gain registers; siblings I-05065, I-02889 dropped; Phase B N-04 reaches 0.5 fF at 1 V.

key_insight: Idle display lines bring depreciated capex, IGZO know-how and no EUV or crucibles; F=0.5 um at 8F2 does give ~62 GB/m2 per tier.
killer_doubt: Display fabs have no ArF; panel steppers resolve ~1.2-1.5 um. At 1.5 um, 8F2 gives ~7 GB/m2 per tier, ~$20/GB at ~$150/m2. Duplicate of I-00145.
decisive_experiment: Settled by I-00145's single-tier panel run, plus a vendor resolution and overlay demo of the best Gen-8.5 stepper at 0.5-0.8 um (~$50k).
prior_art: SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM; Phase B N-38 panel oxide memory; siblings I-10785, I-04673, I-03879; ram-venture A1-03 killed display-glass memory at 2 um.

key_insight: Block codes that tolerate 1% defective cells relax panel-scale defect density, the right lever for huge glass substrates.
killer_doubt: At F=1 um a ~12F2 gain cell gives ~10 GB/m2 per tier; at ~$150/m2 per tier that is ~$15/GB, ~10x DDR5's $1.48 cost. Stacking does not lower $/GB.
decisive_experiment: Settled by I-00145's single-tier panel run; the 1%-defect block-code part is an FPGA study on measured panel defect maps.
prior_art: Weimer TFT (RCA, 1962); SEL CAAC-IGZO memories; memory-in-pixel LCDs; Phase B N-34 defect-budget co-design; sibling I-03879 dropped at 2 um.

key_insight: Transistor-written IGZO gain cells keep endurance unlimited; a bonded Si controller replaces slow TFT periphery; depreciated Gen-8.5 lines add EUV-free supply in ~2 years, not 3-5.
killer_doubt: Cost scales per tier: ~$100-150/m2 per IGZO tier at ~16 GB/m2 (F=0.8 um, 12F2) is ~$6-9/GB, 4-6x DDR5 cost; viable only while contract stays >$10/GB.
decisive_experiment: Buy one tier on a Gen-4.5/6 IGZO pilot line (~$500k): 0.8-1 um 2T0C arrays with a bonded Si sense chiplet; measure bit yield, 85 C retention, access time and real $/m2.
prior_art: SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM; Phase B N-36 glass carriers and N-38 panel memory; sibling I-10785 advanced; I-02880 Si-chiplet sensing.

key_insight: Directional eutectic solidification makes billions of aligned conductors in one thermal step, with no etch or fill: a genuinely unused route to vertical structure.
killer_doubt: Jackson-Hunt (lambda^2 v = const): shrinking micron rod spacing to ~100 nm needs ~100-400x faster growth, metres per hour. Bare rods touch Si, so dielectric still needs an annulus etch.
decisive_experiment: None needed to drop. If pursued: laser-zone-melt Si-TaSi2 films at cm/s and measure rod pitch, order and 85 C junction leakage (~$100k).
prior_art: Si-TaSi2 in-situ eutectic composites for field-emission and junction devices (Ditchek, GTE Labs, 1980s, training knowledge); none as memory plates found.

key_insight: At ~55% porosity, oxidised porous Si fills its own volume (no net expansion), and B at 1e19 adds only ~5e-5 lattice strain: tier count escapes the SiGe strain limit.
killer_doubt: Mesopores in p+ Si are ~10-20 nm, comparable to 20-30 nm sacrificial layers; boron-rich oxide dopes 30 nm device layers (sqrt(Dt) ~9 nm per hour at 850 C).
decisive_experiment: Epi 8-16 Si/Si:B bilayers at 30-60 nm (~$150k, university epi plus anodisation): lateral porosification reach and selectivity from slits, post-oxidation SIMS boron profiles, device-layer mobility.
prior_art: FIPOS (Imai, NTT, 1981) and Canon ELTRAN porous-Si SOI; Phase B N-45 Si/Si:B superlattice; imec and Samsung Si/SiGe 3D DRAM stacks.

key_insight: 1970s NMOS DRAMs proved n-only periphery; 2T0C cells give >1e3 read-current ratios, so 100-300 mV TFT offsets still sense. Memory on any logic BEOL, no Si periphery.
killer_doubt: IGZO PBTI and hydrogen drift of ~50-100 mV over 1e10+ periphery cycles at 85-105 C, and ~3-5x Si periphery area per tier, may cut array efficiency to ~25-35%.
decisive_experiment: University BEOL IGZO run (~$400k): 4-16 kb 2T0C macro with bootstrapped n-only decoders and auto-zeroed latch sensing; measure 50-100 ns access, offset and drift after 1e10 cycles at 105 C.
prior_art: 1970s NMOS DRAMs; IGZO gate-driver-on-array; SEL DOSRAM uses Si periphery; no all-oxide-periphery macro found (via search snippet); Phase B N-35, N-27.

key_insight: Interposer BEOL runs cool and idle under GPU and HBM; oxide cells there give sub-pJ/bit micro-bump access with no TSVs. A passive interposer needs I-02936-style periphery.
killer_doubt: Flagship GPUs moved to CoWoS-L (organic RDL plus Si bridges), shrinking the host. Realistic 6F2 1T1C at 40 nm, 50% efficiency: ~50 Mb/mm2 per tier, ~30-40 GB, not 100.
decisive_experiment: Add a one-tier oxide 1T1C/2T0C block to a 65 nm-class interposer shuttle (~$300k); measure retention and yield after TSV, micro-bump and die-attach thermal steps at 85 C.
prior_art: Phase B N-50 (same idea, ALIVE); TSMC eDTC deep-trench capacitors in CoWoS interposers; active base dies (Intel Foveros).
